citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering seven mathematical reasoning types and five primary tasks across diverse visual contexts including natural images, geometry diagrams, charts, and plots.
name: MathVista
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (each example in the new datasets and VQA labeling was independently annotated by three reviewers; human performance evaluation used 5 annotators per question)
rai:annotatorDemographics: New dataset annotators: graduate students in STEM fields. Human performance evaluators (AMT): workers with a history of completing more than 5,000 HIT tasks and an acceptance score higher than 0.99, required to have a high school diploma or higher. Workers were asked to provide information about their highest level of educational attainment.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For VQA mathematical reasoning labeling: Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial inter-annotator agreement. For the three new datasets: inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2% (only 6 out of 736 newly collected questions exhibited disagreements). For automatic mathematical reasoning category annotation: 94.1% of examples had the exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations; 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in paper figures). Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for human performance evaluation on the testmini subset.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For VQA dataset labeling: three expert annotators manually labeled examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning, using detailed instructions and a custom annotation tool. Annotators chose Yes, No, or Unsure. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA): all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved through discussion. For mathematical reasoning category labeling: expert annotators manually labeled 1,000 examples from seven reasoning type candidates using a custom annotation tool.
rai:dataBiases: Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. The dataset contains 6.57% non-English questions (including Chinese and Persian), requiring models to handle multiple languages. The distribution of mathematical reasoning types is uneven (arithmetic 34.1%, statistical 30.5%, algebraic 28.5%, geometry 23.3%, numeric common sense 14.0%, scientific 10.7%, logical 3.8%). The testmini subset was carefully sampled to closely mirror the full test set distribution (KL Divergence 0.008, TV distance 0.035).
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was collected from three sources: (1) Nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings (2,666 examples), including GPS, MWP, and TQA datasets, each limited to up to 400 examples. (2) Nineteen general VQA datasets (2,739 examples) selected from over 70 reviewed datasets using heuristic rules to identify math-related instances, followed by expert human labeling. (3) Three newly created datasets — IQTest (228 examples), FunctionQA (400 examples), and PaperQA (107 examples) — annotated by graduate students in STEM fields.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets) and newly sourced content: IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms; FunctionQA from functional plots; PaperQA from academic paper figures (tables, figures, charts) from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. The dataset was published at ICLR 2024 (arXiv submission October 2023).
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset coverage may have gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning specific domains (science, college-level math) makes data collection labor-intensive, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations due to heterogeneous source datasets; annotations lack a unified format and structure. The benchmark focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models at time of publication.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were applied to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning: examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words (e.g., most, least, mean, average, ratio, percent, etc.) were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets (e.g., refining potential data noise) in response to community feedback, and to evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MathVista is intended to drive development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, with applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The benchmark highlights a significant gap between current AI models and human performance, underscoring the need for further model improvements.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of LLMs and LMMs in visual contexts; benchmarking foundation models on tasks requiring fine-grained visual understanding and compositional reasoning; facilitating development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios; model development validation (testmini subset); standard evaluation (test subset via online evaluation platform).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor to extract short answer text from detailed model responses (achieving >99.5% accuracy on a preliminary study of 200 examples). EasyOCR (JaidedAI, 2020) was used to detect OCR text from images for augmented LLM experiments. Multimodal Bard was used to generate image captions for augmented LLM experiments.
